name: How do you properly tape and mud drywall in high-moisture bathrooms?

mainEntity.name: How do you properly tape and mud drywall in high-moisture bathrooms?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom drywall installation requires moisture-resistant joint compound or setting-type compounds rather than standard lightweight all-purpose mud for foundational coats. Setting-type compound (hot mud) hardens through chemical reaction rather than evaporation, providing a denser, moisture-resilient bond that resists high humidity. All joints should be taped using fiberglass mesh tape or mold-resistant paper tape embedded firmly to prevent bubbling. A final coat of moisture-resistant primer must seal the entire surface before applying bathroom-grade paint formulated with antimicrobial additives to protect the paper face.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use setting-type compound or moisture-resistant mud with mold-resistant tape, followed by thorough drying, smooth sanding, and an antimicrobial primer.
